newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Down on aggressive offers.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Down on aggressive offers.

text.p: Singapore gas oil and jet prices fell on aggressive offers despite a spate of buy tenders from India, traders said on Wednesday.

Near market close, 150,000 barrels of gas oil for May 8-12 loading was sold by a U.S major to a local trader at $27.00 per barrel and another cargo sold by a western trader to the same buyer for May 19-23 loading at $26.50.
A 100,000 barrels of jet for May 19-23 loading was also traded, sold by a European major to a local trader at $24.60.
Traders said gas oil offers were aggressive in the cash market with sellers undercutting each other by offering lower levels.
They said a spate of import tender from India failed to support prices.

India has issued three one-year term tenderS to buy high speed diesel for delivery between June 1997 to May 1998. It seeks a total of 36 cargoes of 0.25 percent and 1.0 percent for delivery between 1-7 and/or 16-23 of each month.
It has also issued a spot tender to buy 0.25 percent and 1.0 percent diesel for delivery in June. The tender will close April 29 and will be valid until May 1.
Traders said gas oil demand from China remained lacklustre. They said bids were too low and China has been consistently taking May barrels from Hong Kong and South Korea.
Bids from Chinese buyers were under $200 per tonne, c+f south China.
Traders said the gas oil market is a tad soft with brimming inventories in Singapore. They said potential arbitrage cargoes is also putting pressure on prices.

On the jet fuel/kerosene market, India has also issued a one-year term tender to buy superior kerosene for delivery from June 1997 to May 1998. The tender would close on April 23 and is valid until May 3.
